newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-PALMER REVEALS HE HAS PROSTATE CANCER.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-PALMER REVEALS HE HAS PROSTATE CANCER.

text.p: Arnold Palmer, who won seven major championships and lifted golf's popularity to unprecedented heights four decades ago, revealed he has prostate cancer and will not play competitively while undergoing treatment.
Palmer announced during the PGA Tour Awards dinner on Friday night at Carlsbad, California, that he was diagnosed with prostate cancer after undergoing a biopsy on Thursday.
The 67-year-old Palmer officially withdrew from next week's Bob Hope Classic and said he doubts he will be playing golf "until this thing is taken care of."
Prostate cancer is a slow-developing cancer that can be successfully treated if detected early.

Palmer, one of the most recognisable athletes in professional sports over the last four decades, won four Masters titles, two British Opens and one U.S. Open in his legendary career. He ranks fourth on the all-time PGA Tour victory list with 60 titles and has won 10 Senior Tournaments.
The Mercedes Championship golf tournament is underway in Carlsbad, although Palmer is not playing in the event.
